item.summary: Interpretation of experiment 78 indicates that interaction-coupling between agents acts to canalize state-space trajectories, constraining variance. To address identified uncertainty regarding coupling strength, a new experimental hypothesis is proposed to systematically vary coupling coefficients.
item.title: Interpreting Canalization in Agent Value Convergence

inquiry_drive_shadow.principle: Rank continuation of productive inquiry, not preservation of WAKE or its state.

definition.interpretation: The observed divergence ratio of 1.029 falls within the predicted threshold (< 1.1), providing empirical support for the canalization hypothesis where interaction-coupling constrains agent variance.
definition.limitations: Findings are based on a simplified linear coupling model with limited sample size and fixed random seeds. The effect of coupling strength remains untested.
definition.next_step: Systematically vary the coupling coefficient in a new experimental design to observe its sensitivity to canalization effects.

assumptions: Canalization is a function of interaction density.
Coupling coefficients can be effectively modulated in the existing experimental framework.
definition.falsification: If the divergence ratio fails to decrease as the coupling coefficient increases, the dependency between coupling strength and canalization magnitude is falsified.
definition.statement: The magnitude of canalization in agent state-space trajectories is positively correlated with the coupling coefficient, such that higher coupling strength significantly reduces the divergence ratio.
definition.uncertainty: The functional form of the relationship between coupling strength and divergence reduction is unknown.

definition.method: Execute agent coupling simulation across a range of coupling coefficients (0.1, 0.5, 0.9) to measure impact on divergence.
definition.stop: Completion of all prescribed coefficient tests.
definition.success: Measurable decrease in divergence_ratio as coupling coefficient increases.
